subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU type and TPS targets
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU type and TPS targets

Hi Sanjay — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can put together a sizing + pricing recommendation for Dedicated capacity.

Recap from our discussion:
- Use case: realtime customer support summarization + short-form content generation (low-latency, high-availability).
- Likely deployment: Dedicated capacity (preferred) with VPC peering into FinTechCorp VPC later for production.
- Models discussed: MPT/LLM-family 30B
70B (quantized), occasional heavier batches for fine-tuning inference.

What we need to finalize sizing
1) Expected peak TPS (requests/sec) and typical/average TPS. If you can give both sustained and burst numbers, that helps.
2) Concurrency per user/request (how many parallel sessions typically hitting the model?)
3) Token mix: average input tokens and average output tokens per request (or representative samples).
4) Any strict P95 latency SLO (e.g., <200ms) and max acceptable tail latency.
5) Preferred cloud/hardware (GCP vs AWS) and any preference for H100 vs A100 if you have one.

From the call notes I captured in the attached spreadsheet (RDW-dedicated-sku-estimates.xlsx) we sketched two scenarios: conservative (lower-cost A100 baseline) and performance-first (H100 for headroom). We can tune further once we have the numbers above and a short traffic sample (JSON lines or logs).

Next steps
- If you can reply with the TPS and token mix this afternoon, we’ll return a preliminary sizing and cost estimate by EOD tomorrow.
- If preferred, we can schedule a deeper sizing meeting with our SREs and solutions engineers (30–45 mins).

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@fintechcorp.com>

Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@fintechcorp.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU type and TPS targets

Thanks Rafael — good recap. A few answers inline below and a couple of clarifications.

TPS and concurrency
- Peak TPS (requests/sec): ~50 requests/sec during business hours (estimated 10:00–16:00 PT).
- Average TPS: ~8–12 requests/sec across the day.
- Typical concurrency: Many requests are short single-turn queries; concurrent long-running sessions expected to be ~8–12 concurrent model calls at a time.

Token mix
- Average input tokens: ~30 tokens
- Average output tokens: ~120 tokens
- We do have occasional long-generation jobs (~1k output tokens) but they are <5% of overall traffic and can be batched/offloaded to a non-low-latency path.

Latency SLO
- Target P95 latency: <=300ms is ideal; <=500ms is acceptable for most flows. For a subset of flows (first-turn greeting/resolution) we’d like <250ms where possible.

Cloud/hardware
- Preference: GCP is preferred for our infra. We don’t have a strict H100 requirement but want guidance on cost vs. headroom.

Other notes
- We can provide a 48-hour sample of traffic logs (anonymized) — Priya will send that once we confirm how to format.
- Security: we will need VPC peering and SOC2 evidence — happy to parallelize that work once sizing and cost look reasonable.

Can you put together a preliminary sizing (H100 vs A100, node counts) and a suggested next time for a deep-dive meeting?

Thanks — Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Applied ML, FinTechCorp
sanjay@fintechcorp.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 12:00:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU type and TPS targets

Looping you both in with Sanjay's numbers. Quick thoughts before we respond to the customer:
- Peak 50 rps, avg 10, token mix 30/120 with ~5% long runs. Target p95 <=300–500ms. GCP preferred.
- Recommend we propose two options: cost-optimized (A100 80GB quantized) and performance/headroom (H100 80GB).
- Preliminary sizing idea (very rough):
  * A100 option: 4x A100 GPUs (single-node pod with 4 GPUs) serving quantized 70B model with autoscale to 8 GPUs for burst; should hit baseline but might be tight on P95 during peak.
  * H100 option: 4x H100 GPUs baseline (or 2 nodes x 2 GPUs each) with better tail latency and lower model sharding overhead for 70B.
- We need SRE to validate memory/kv cache sizing (Marissa) and an inference perf run on representative prompts.

Attaching my quick notes. Can you each add sizing comments and we’ll send a consolidated reply + proposed meeting slot (Wed/Thu next week)?

Thanks — Rafael

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU type and TPS targets

Hi Sanjay / Priya — thanks for the details and for offering the traffic sample. Based on the numbers Rafael shared, here's a concise preliminary recommendation and next steps.

Prelim sizing (ballpark)
- Workload: quantized 70B-class model (production-quality responses, moderate generation length).
- Recommended baseline: 2 nodes with 4x H100 (80GB) total across the cluster (can be arranged as 1 node with 4 GPUs or 2 nodes x 2 GPUs depending on GCP SKU availability).
  * Rationale: H100 gives better sequence-parallel efficiency and lower p95 tail for the token mix you described. It also provides headroom for short bursts without immediate autoscaling.
- Cost-optimized alternative: 4x A100 (80GB) with aggressive batching and KV prefix caching. This reduces cost but may need autoscale during peak; expect slightly higher P95.

Operational asks
- Please send the 48-hour anonymized traffic sample (JSONL preferred) and one representative prompt set. That will let us run a perf test against your prompt distribution.
- Confirm whether the occasional long jobs (>1k tokens) can be routed to a separate batch queue. If yes, that significantly lowers baseline needs.
- If you want VPC peering and SOC2 intake in parallel, let us know and we’ll loop our security team.

Next steps / scheduling
- I propose a 45-minute sizing deep-dive with our SREs and performance engineers to validate estimates and run through KV cache/replication. Suggested slots: Wed 07/29 10:00–10:45 PT or Thu 07/30 13:00–13:45 PT.
- We’ll include a preliminary cost estimate and a short runbook for trialing Dedicated capacity (1-week baseline trial).

If those times work, Rafael or Dylan can lock the calendar and we’ll send an agenda.

Best — Marissa
